title: I Love a Mystery
paragraphs: Carlton E. Morse’s serialized mystery-adventure series follows Jack Packard, Doc Long, and their companions through long-form cases filled with danger, crime, and the uncanny.

Carlton E. Morse serialized mystery-adventure about Jack Packard, Doc Long, Reggie Yorke and later Jerry Booker. Frozen GRH snapshot has 159 playable serial chapters from 1939-1952, including two undated mislabeled duplicate files in the Graves of Whamperjaw serial.

GRH documents the program through NBC West Coast daily serial (January 16, 1939 to September 29, 1939) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], National NBC daily serial (October 2, 1939 to March 29, 1940) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], NBC/Blue weekly half-hour era (April 4, 1940 to June 29, 1942) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], and CBS weekday serial (March 22, 1943 to December 29, 1944) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Jim Boles (performer on 84 recordings), Russell Thorson (performer on 81 recordings), Carleton E. Morse (writer on 76 recordings, creator on 75 recordings, producer on 69 recordings, and director on 4 recordings), Frank McCarthy (announcer on 73 recordings), Tony Randall (performer on 72 recordings), Mercedes McCambridge (performer on 67 recordings), and Barton Yarborough (performer on 11 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.41e846edb6a1b781|KALW-FM]] (originated at station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include international travel and remote settings, murder and violent crime, vampires, supernatural and uncanny threats, detective work and investigation, and war and military conflict.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Network mystery-adventure serial culture, Postwar revival through script reuse, Reggie Yorke removed after Walter Paterson death, and I Love Adventure continuation.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (13 shared credited people), [[show|the-mysterious-traveler|The Mysterious Traveler]] (7 shared credited people), [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]] (6 shared credited people), [[show|let-george-do-it|Let George Do It]] (7 shared credited people), and [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (6 shared credited people).
